findings.title: should_block? has DB write side effects and double counts per attempt
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count and calls record.save whenever a matching record is found. EmailValidator calls it during User validation; UsersController#create calls user.valid? before user.save, and save runs validations again, so one blocked signup attempt increments and saves the BlockedEmail row twice. The read-modify-write is also not atomic, so concurrent attempts can lose increments. Track match statistics after a real signup attempt (or use an atomic update) and avoid writing in a validation predicate.

findings.title: Blocked email lookup is case-sensitive and unnormalized
findings.body: BlockedEmail.should_block? uses BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first with the raw submitted value. Elsewhere the app normalizes email addresses via Email.downcase (and change_email also strips), but this check does not. On PostgreSQL the unique index is case-sensitive, so a block stored as foo@example.com can be bypassed by submitting Foo@example.com, and duplicate case-variant block records can be created. Normalize the address before lookup and before persistence.

findings.title: change_email sends confirmation for blocked email before validation
findings.body: change_email creates an EmailToken for lower_email and enqueues the authorize_email job without checking BlockedEmail.should_block? or otherwise running email validation. Because the new block validator only runs when a User record's email is changed and saved, a blocked email can receive a confirmation/authorization email before any model validation occurs. Add an explicit BlockedEmail check in change_email and reject the request before creating the token or enqueuing mail.

findings.title: rejectedEmails is shared mutable state and never reset
findings.body: Defining rejectedEmails: Em.A([]) on the controller class creates one shared Ember array rather than a per-instance array. Because createAccount only pushes into it and there is no clearing on successful account creation or modal close, an email rejected during one attempt remains rejected for later attempts in the same long-lived controller instance. Define the array in init or clear it when the signup form is reset.

findings.title: Any server email error is cached as rejected, not just block-list failures
findings.body: On a failed create, any presence of result.errors.email causes result.values.email to be pushed into rejectedEmails. Server errors can include uniqueness (already has been taken), domain whitelist/blacklist, blocked-list, or other failures, but the client will later show every such address as user.email.invalid. It also never removes entries. Cache only a machine-readable blocked-email rejection or clear rejectedEmails after the specific issue is resolved.
